summary.title: Medication Dispenser - Corrected STRIDE Model
summary.description: Medication dispensing threat model with authenticated doctors, independent admin approval of doctor-patient assignments, per-request authorization, audit logging, and safe dispensing. Controls are design requirements, not verified deployment facts.

diagrams.title: 01 - Central System and Doctor Permissions
diagrams.description: Medication dispenser cybersecurity data-flow model. Links between the two diagrams: Central API and Dispenser Software communicate using authenticated and protected requests.

cells.description: Healthcare professional requests assignment and prescription changes.
Authorized independent approver of doctor-patient assignments.
Verifies clinician and administrator credentials against user accounts. Issues authenticated session after successful login.

threats.title: Stolen staff credentials
threats.description: An attacker logs in using compromised staff credentials.
threats.mitigation: MFA, rate limiting, secure password handling, alerting and credential revocation.

cells.description: Verifies each session token, obtains trustworthy user identity and routes authorized requests.

threats.title: Bypass authentication on API
threats.description: An unauthenticated or expired session attempts protected requests.
threats.mitigation: Enforce authentication on every protected endpoint and reject invalid/expired tokens.

cells.description: Checks authenticated doctor-patient assignment and allowed action for each prescription modification.

threats.title: Change another patient prescription
threats.description: A doctor tries to modify an unassigned patient prescription.
threats.mitigation: Perform server-side doctor-patient access checks for each operation, including update transactions.

cells.description: Applies change only with authorization matching doctor, patient and operation; checks medication data.

threats.title: Prescription tampering
threats.description: An attacker manipulates doses, timing or drugs.
threats.mitigation: Check authenticated permissions, input constraints, clinical safety rules and independent review for high-risk changes.

cells.description: Records a pending request to become responsible for a specific patient; does not confer prescribing access.
Verifies independent administrator role and approval; blocks self-approval before activating assignment.

threats.title: Self-approved doctor assignment
threats.description: A doctor approves their own assignment and obtains access to someone else’s prescriptions.
threats.mitigation: Require a separately authenticated authorized approver, separation of duties and audited decisions.

cells.description: Stores doctors, patients, accounts/credential hashes, doctor-patient assignments, pending requests, prescriptions and schedules.
Records authentication, rejected access, prescription edits, assignment requests/approvals and dispensing events.

threats.title: Altered or deleted audit records
threats.description: An attacker changes or removes evidence of unauthorized prescription modifications.
threats.mitigation: Use restricted append-only audit logging, integrity protections, retention and monitoring.

threats.mitigation: Use HTTPS, short-lived tokens, secure cookie flags, session revocation and MFA.

diagrams.title: 02 - Dispenser and Patient Safety
diagrams.description: Medication dispenser cybersecurity data-flow model. Links between the two diagrams: Central API and Dispenser Software communicate using authenticated and protected requests.

cells.description: Patient identifies at the dispenser and requests a scheduled dose.
Verifies the patient identity through card/PIN and maps it to a patient record.
Retrieves current patient medication schedule only after server-side patient access checks.
Checks right patient, medication, amount, time, duplicate dispensing and safe device state before granting dispense permission.

threats.title: Incorrect dose authorized
threats.description: An unsafe dose or repeated dispense is approved due to stale or altered instructions.
threats.mitigation: Verify prescription version and validity, prevent duplicate events, enforce dosing limits and fail safely.

cells.description: Activates hardware only on a valid approved dose and reports result; does not dispense on communication or validation failures.

threats.title: Unauthorized medication dispense
threats.description: An attacker forges an approval command or manipulates the dispensing mechanism.
threats.mitigation: Enforce authenticated commands, local safety interlocks, anti-replay protection and hardware monitoring.
